task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, create a pie chart from these synthetic trip records. Each record lists district, day type, travel mode, and trip count. Multiple records for the same mode are separate batches and should be added together.

Central, weekday, Bus, 20
Central, weekday, Bus, 40
Central, weekday, Bicycle, 10
Central, weekday, Bicycle, 20
Central, weekday, Walking, 4
Central, weekday, Walking, 6
Central, weekend, Bus, 90
Central, weekend, Bicycle, 5
Central, weekend, Walking, 5
West, weekday, Bus, 10
West, weekday, Bicycle, 80
West, weekday, Walking, 10

Keep only weekday records from Central. Sum the trip counts by travel mode and calculate each mode's percentage of the total trips in those retained records. Draw one slice per mode. Label each slice with its mode and percentage to one decimal place. Use blue for Bus, orange for Bicycle, and green for Walking. Use the title 'Weekday travel in Central' and equal axis scaling so the pie is circular. Use a 6 by 5 inch figure at 150 DPI. Keep all text fully visible and readable, and save figure.png.

function.arguments:
{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > create_pie_chart.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Parse the synthetic trip records
records = [
    ("Central", "weekday", "Bus", 20),
    ("Central", "weekday", "Bus", 40),
    ("Central", "weekday", "Bicycle", 10),
    ("Central", "weekday", "Bicycle", 20),
    ("Central", "weekday", "Walking", 4),
    ("Central", "weekday", "Walking", 6),
    ("Central", "weekend", "Bus", 90),
    ("Central", "weekend", "Bicycle", 5),
    ("Central", "weekend", "Walking", 5),
    ("West", "weekday", "Bus", 10),
    ("West", "weekday", "Bicycle", 80),
    ("West", "weekday", "Walking", 10),
]

# Filter to keep only weekday records from Central
weekday_central_records = [
    (district, day_type, mode, count)
    for district, day_type, mode, count in records
    if district == "Central" and day_type == "weekday"
]

# Sum trip counts by travel mode
mode_counts = {}
for district, day_type, mode, count in weekday_central_records:
    mode_counts[mode] = mode_counts.get(mode, 0) + count

# Calculate total trips
total_trips = sum(mode_counts.values())

# Calculate percentages
mode_percentages = {
    mode: (count / total_trips) * 100
    for mode, count in mode_counts.items()
}

# Prepare data for plotting
modes = list(mode_percentages.keys())
percentages = [mode_percentages[mode] for mode in modes]
colors = {
    "Bus": "blue",
    "Bicycle": "orange",
    "Walking": "green"
}
color_list = [colors[mode] for mode in modes]

# Create pie chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5), dpi=150)

# Create labels with mode and percentage
labels = [f"{mode}\n{percentage:.1f}%" for mode, percentage in zip(modes, percentages)]

# Create pie chart
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(
    percentages,
    labels=labels,
    colors=color_list,
    autopct=None,  # We'll use our own labels
    startangle=90,
    pctdistance=0.85,
    labeldistance=1.05
)

# Set title
ax.set_title("Weekday travel in Central")

# Equal aspect ratio ensures the pie is circular
ax.axis('equal')

# Adjust text properties for better readability
for text in texts:
    text.set_fontsize(10)
    text.set_fontweight('bold')

for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_fontsize(9)
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("Pie chart saved as figure.png")
EOF
"}
